Is it shopping, dining, entertainment, fuel, travel or a combination of these categories? The ideal or best Credit Card for you therefore would be the one that is tailored to your requirements in terms of your spending habits, lifestyle goals and the credit limit you are seeking. The ultimate aim is to optimise available rewards and benefits while also considering applicable fees and interest rates.If you are a first time Credit Card holder, consider the following factors before choosing your Credit Card:Monthly expenses: Choose a Credit Card whose limit is close to your monthly expenses. If you have a lower credit limit, prioritise only the payments which should be made through your Credit Card.Rewards & Points: You could also select a Credit Card that offers certain additional benefits such as cashback and discounts on your purchases or complimentary access to airport lounges.Card control: Choose the card issuer based on how easy it is to manage the Credit Card especially on the mobile app or website. You should be able to manage spend limit, international usage, set the PlN, view payment history & statements, block & replace card, among other features.Card offers: Apart from offers from brands and merchants, card issuers also offer other benefits such as converting spends into EMIs, availing instant loans, upgrading card limit, getting an add-on card for your family members, and much more.Card fees and charges: Credit Cards will have slightly different interest rates depending on the issuer that offers the card. Therefore, always compare the fees and interest rates before you choose a Credit Card.Things to know before applying for a Credit CardIf you are a first time Credit Card holder or are planning to apply for one, here’s what you should know before choosing your Credit Card: Monthly spends: Select a Credit Card whose credit limit aligns closely with your monthly spending.Maximising benefits: Reap maximum benefits by choosing a Credit Card that offers certain additional benefits such as cashback and discounts on your purchases or complimentary access to airport lounges.Credit Card eligibility: If you have applied for an Axis Bank Credit Card, your eligibility will depend largely on the following factors: 1. Age 2. Income 3. Residential status (whether you are an Indian resident or NRI). You will have to show documents as proof of the above mentioned eligibility conditions. Documents required will include - Age and Residential proof (PAN card, Aadhaar card, Passport or Driver’s license), income proof (Salary slips or Income Tax Returns). Additionally, the bank may also look at your credit score and credit history to determine if you are eligible for a Credit Card.Fees and Charges: Credit Cards have certain fees that vary depending on the card variant you hold. Some common Credit Card fees include joining fees, annual fees, late payment fees, over-limit penalties, cash withdrawal fees, rent transaction fees, foreign currency transaction fees, etc.Interest Rates: If you repay your Credit Card dues in full every month, before the due date, then you don’t have to pay an interest rate on your Credit Card outstanding amount. But if you carry forward any amount of your Credit Card due, then you do incur an interest rate on the pending amount. This interest rate on Credit Cards is typically between 3% and 4% monthly. Tips to manage your Credit Card expensesIf you are a first time Credit Card holder or are planning to apply for one, here’s what you should know before choosing your Credit Card:Keep an eye on your spending Consistently tracking your spending can help you resist the urge to overspend. Additionally, you can set transaction limits using the “manage spends” feature for specific purchases on your Credit Card, making it easier for you to adhere to your spending objectives. Don’t use your entire Credit Card limitIdeally you should aim for spending not more than 30% of your Credit Card limit. You can control your spending and avoid debt by doing so.Check Credit Card statements regularlyRegularly checking your statement helps you stay on top of your spending, ensure accurate billing, detect fraudulent activity and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. Pay your Credit Card bills on timeThis helps you maintain a good credit score and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. You can also set up automatic payment or payment reminders to help you pay your bill before due date. You should also opt for paying your dues in full and not just the minimum amount due in order to avoid interest charges.Use your Credit Card points and offersUsing available offers and rewards is an excellent way to maximise the benefits of your Credit Card and save money on every purchase. What is Credit Card? A Credit Card allows you to borrow money for your purchases and is like a short-term loan from a bank. Also known as plastic money, you can use this card to buy things and have the option to pay the borrowed money back all at once or in smaller amounts over time. Yes, using a credit card can impact your credit score positively or negatively, depending on how you manage it. Here’s how: Positive impact:Timely payments: Paying your credit card bills on or before the due date improves your credit history and boosts your score. Low credit utilization: Keeping your spending well below your credit limit (ideally under 30%) shows responsible usage. Long-term usage: Maintaining a credit card account for a long time adds to your credit history length, which is good for your score. Negative impact: Late or missed payments: Delays in payment can significantly reduce your score and attract penalties. High credit utilization: Consistently using most of your credit limit may signal financial stress and lower your score. Multiple new cards: Applying for too many cards in a short period can lead to hard inquiries, which may temporarily reduce your score. Key Tip: Using a credit card responsibly is one of the easiest ways to build and maintain a healthy credit score. Always pay on time and keep your utilization low. 17. Don’t use your entire Credit Card limitIdeally you should aim for spending not more than 30% of your Credit Card limit. You can control your spending and avoid debt by doing so.Check Credit Card statements regularlyRegularly checking your statement helps you stay on top of your spending, ensure accurate billing, detect fraudulent activity and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. Pay your Credit Card bills on timeThis helps you maintain a good credit score and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. You can also set up automatic payment or payment reminders to help you pay your bill before due date. You should also opt for paying your dues in full and not just the minimum amount due in order to avoid interest charges.Use your Credit Card points and offersUsing available offers and rewards is an excellent way to maximise the benefits of your Credit Card and save money on every purchase. To know more about the program, please refer to the terms and conditions.

On every successful credit card referral (A ‘successful credit card referral’ means that the referred person has applied according to the terms of the campaign and has been issued a credit card by Axis Bank) through this referral program, the referrer will receive Gift Vouchers.

What is Credit Card? A Credit Card allows you to borrow money for your purchases and is like a short-term loan from a bank. Also known as plastic money, you can use this card to buy things and have the option to pay the borrowed money back all at once or in smaller amounts over time. However, if you don't pay the full amount right away, you are charged an extra amount on it in the form of interest. 2. What is the minimum credit score for a credit card? The credit card limit, which is set by the bank, represents the maximum amount you can spend using your credit card. It is determined by considering various factors such as income, age, credit history, credit score, liabilities, etc. It is essential to ensure that the total expenditure, including fees, stays within this predetermined limit. What is a credit card limit? The credit card limit is the maximum amount you can spend on your credit card and is set by the bank. The total amount spent, including the fees, should be within this limit. Factors like income, age, credit history, credit score, liability etc. determine your credit card limit. To read more click on https://www.axis.bank.in/blogs/credit-card/what-is-credit-card-limit-and-how-to-increase-your-credit-limit 15. Is there a fixed limit for all cards? There is no single fixed limit for all cards; it's a unique amount for each cardholder that can be checked by logging into the Mobile Banking App, open or internet banking and navigating to the account summary or control center. To know about the maximum limit on the credit card, read https://www.axis.bank.in/blogs/credit-card/what-is-maximum-credit-limit-on-a-credit-card 16. Will using a credit card affect my credit score? Yes, using a credit card can impact your credit score positively or negatively, depending on how you manage it. Here’s how: Positive impact:Timely payments: Paying your credit card bills on or before the due date improves your credit history and boosts your score. Low credit utilization: Keeping your spending well below your credit limit (ideally under 30%) shows responsible usage. Long-term usage: Maintaining a credit card account for a long time adds to your credit history length, which is good for your score. Negative impact: Late or missed payments: Delays in payment can significantly reduce your score and attract penalties. High credit utilization: Consistently using most of your credit limit may signal financial stress and lower your score. Multiple new cards: Applying for too many cards in a short period can lead to hard inquiries, which may temporarily reduce your score. Key Tip: Using a credit card responsibly is one of the easiest ways to build and maintain a healthy credit score. Always pay on time and keep your utilization low. 17. Step 3: Tap on the ‘Manage Usage’ option. Step 4: Finally, choose the ‘International’ option and turn on the ‘International Usage’ option. Your credit card is now ready to be used internationally. Net banking: Step 1: Login and click on Services > Credit Card Services. Step 2: Post this, select your credit card and click on ‘Manage Usage’ option. Then you can enable international transactions for your credit card here. 7. How to prepare for international use? Enable international transactions: For new cards, you must enable online, contactless, and international transaction functionalities through the Mobile Banking App, open, internet banking, or by contacting customer support before your travel. Check for fees:Understand the foreign transaction fees and Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) fees on your specific card. For example, some cards have a DCC markup fee of 1% plus taxes on transactions in INR at international locations. Avoid restricted transactions: You cannot use the card for payments to overseas Forex trading platforms, as this is prohibited by regulations. Note on Nepal and Bhutan: Your credit card is not valid for making foreign currency transactions in Nepal and Bhutan. 8. What to expect when using your card abroad? Foreign transaction fee: A fee is often charged by the credit card network for currency conversion. Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) fee: If the merchant offers to charge you in your home currency (INR), you may be subject to a DCC fee, which is often higher than using the foreign currency directly. It is generally better to be charged in the local currency and let your bank handle the conversion. Cash advances: Taking cash from overseas ATMs can incur extra charges and higher interest rates. Taxes: Be aware that taxes may apply to international fees like DCC markup fees. 9. What are the credit card international transaction fees? To understand about the fee and breakdown, read https://www.axis.bank.in/blogs/credit-card/foreign-transaction-fee-on-credit-cards 10. What are the charges for a foreign transaction? The amount of the foreign transaction fee on credit card varies depending on the credit card issuer. Typically, this fee ranges from 1% to 3% of the transaction amount. To know more, visit: https://www.axis.bank.in/blogs/credit-card/foreign-transaction-fee-on-credit-cards Load More 1. What are the possible billing cycle dates for my credit card? The possible billing cycle dates for a credit card statement are as follows: Miles & More Cards – 25th of each month Vistara Cards – 22nd of each month Signature Card – 18th of each month Ace Credit Card – 15th of each month Axis Bank Freecharge Plus Credit Card – 12th of each month Other Cards - 1st,12th,13th,15th,20th,22nd and 25th of every month Miles & More Cards, Flipkart Axis Bank Credit Cards, Ace Credit Card, Axis Bank Freecharge Plus Credit Card & Signature Cards have a fixed billing cycle, other card customers can call us on Phone Numbers 1860-419-5555 (Charges Applicable)/ 1860-500-5555 (Charges Applicable) / 1800-103-5577 (Toll Free Number) or write to us to request for a change in the billing cycle considering the available options. 2. Credit Card billing cycle - What is it and how does it work? To know more about credit card billing cycle, visit https://www.axis.bank.in/blogs/credit-card/credit-card-billing-cycle 3. How do you check your specific billing date? To check your billing cycle date, you can go for one of the following:Axis Bank Mobile App, open or Internet Banking: Log in to Axis Bank Mobile App, open and view your account details and billing cycle information.Customer Care: Call or write to customer support to get information about your specific billing date. Statement: Your statement will show your billing cycle and due date. Load More 1. How to report a lost card? You can report a lost Axis Bank card by calling the 24-hour helpline at +91-22-67987700, using the Axis Mobile App, open or Internet Banking, or by sending an SMS to 5676782 or +919717000002 from a registered number with the message "BLOCKXXXX" (where XXXX are last 4 digits of the card number). By phone: Emergency Helpline: Call +91-22-67987700 from any phone to report the loss. Customer Service (For Forex Card): Call 1800-108-5577 (toll-free) or +91 040 67174100. By mobile or internet banking: Axis Mobile App, open: Log in to the Axis Mobile App, open and go to the credit cards section using ‘quick links’, use the "Block and replace Card" option. Internet Banking: Log in to your Internet Banking account and go to the "Credit Cards" section to block the card. By SMS: SMS format: Send "BLOCKCARD" to 5676782 or +919717000002. Important: Ensure you are using a mobile number that is registered with your Axis Bank account. 2. How do I block my card? If your credit card is lost or stolen, you can block your credit card and order for a replacement by simply entering your registered mobile number. Go to https://application.axis.bank.in/WebForms/axis-support/Block-cccard.aspx and fill in the details. If your debit card is lost or stolen, you can block your debit card and order for a replacement by simply entering your registered mobile number. Go to https://application.axis.bank.in/webforms/axis-support/block-dccard.aspx and fill in the details. 3. What should I do when my credit card is lost? In the event of losing your credit card, promptly notify Axis Bank by contacting customer care. The card will be instantly blocked, and during the same call, you can request a replacement. Additionally, report the lost card to the police station in the area where you suspect it was misplaced or lost. 4. How to block a card if it is lost/stolen? You can block a lost or stolen Axis Bank card by calling the 24/7 customer care number, sending an SMS from your registered mobile number, logging in to Mobile Banking App, open or using net banking. For debit cards, you can SMS "BLOCKCARD" to 5676782 or +919717000002. For credit cards, SMS "BLOCKXXXX" (where XXXX are the last four digits) to 5676782. By phone: Call the customer service helpline: For a debit card, call +91-22-67987700. For a Forex card, call +91 04067174100. Inform the executive: State that you want to block your card and provide the necessary details for verification. By SMS: For debit cards: Type BLOCK CARD and send it to 5676782 or +919717000002 from your registered mobile number. For credit cards: Type BLOCK XXXX (where XXXX is the last four digits of your card) and send it to 5676782 from your registered mobile number. Online: Mobile Banking App, open: Log in to the app to find the option to block your card. Net Banking: Access your account through Axis Bank's website and use the card blocking feature under the card services section. 5. What to do after blocking my card? Once the card is blocked, you can apply for a replacement card through your bank branch, as blocking the card doesn't automatically order a new one. Is it shopping, dining, entertainment, fuel, travel or a combination of these categories? The ideal or best Credit Card for you therefore would be the one that is tailored to your requirements in terms of your spending habits, lifestyle goals and the credit limit you are seeking. The ultimate aim is to optimise available rewards and benefits while also considering applicable fees and interest rates.If you are a first time Credit Card holder, consider the following factors before choosing your Credit Card:Monthly expenses: Choose a Credit Card whose limit is close to your monthly expenses. If you have a lower credit limit, prioritise only the payments which should be made through your Credit Card.Rewards & Points: You could also select a Credit Card that offers certain additional benefits such as cashback and discounts on your purchases or complimentary access to airport lounges.Card control: Choose the card issuer based on how easy it is to manage the Credit Card especially on the mobile app or website. You should be able to manage spend limit, international usage, set the PlN, view payment history & statements, block & replace card, among other features.Card offers: Apart from offers from brands and merchants, card issuers also offer other benefits such as converting spends into EMIs, availing instant loans, upgrading card limit, getting an add-on card for your family members, and much more.Card fees and charges: Credit Cards will have slightly different interest rates depending on the issuer that offers the card. Therefore, always compare the fees and interest rates before you choose a Credit Card.Things to know before applying for a Credit CardIf you are a first time Credit Card holder or are planning to apply for one, here’s what you should know before choosing your Credit Card: Monthly spends: Select a Credit Card whose credit limit aligns closely with your monthly spending.Maximising benefits: Reap maximum benefits by choosing a Credit Card that offers certain additional benefits such as cashback and discounts on your purchases or complimentary access to airport lounges.Credit Card eligibility: If you have applied for an Axis Bank Credit Card, your eligibility will depend largely on the following factors: 1. Age 2. Income 3. Residential status (whether you are an Indian resident or NRI). You will have to show documents as proof of the above mentioned eligibility conditions. Documents required will include - Age and Residential proof (PAN card, Aadhaar card, Passport or Driver’s license), income proof (Salary slips or Income Tax Returns). Additionally, the bank may also look at your credit score and credit history to determine if you are eligible for a Credit Card.Fees and Charges: Credit Cards have certain fees that vary depending on the card variant you hold. Some common Credit Card fees include joining fees, annual fees, late payment fees, over-limit penalties, cash withdrawal fees, rent transaction fees, foreign currency transaction fees, etc.Interest Rates: If you repay your Credit Card dues in full every month, before the due date, then you don’t have to pay an interest rate on your Credit Card outstanding amount. But if you carry forward any amount of your Credit Card due, then you do incur an interest rate on the pending amount. This interest rate on Credit Cards is typically between 3% and 4% monthly. Tips to manage your Credit Card expensesIf you are a first time Credit Card holder or are planning to apply for one, here’s what you should know before choosing your Credit Card:Keep an eye on your spending Consistently tracking your spending can help you resist the urge to overspend. Additionally, you can set transaction limits using the “manage spends” feature for specific purchases on your Credit Card, making it easier for you to adhere to your spending objectives. Don’t use your entire Credit Card limitIdeally you should aim for spending not more than 30% of your Credit Card limit. You can control your spending and avoid debt by doing so.Check Credit Card statements regularlyRegularly checking your statement helps you stay on top of your spending, ensure accurate billing, detect fraudulent activity and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. Pay your Credit Card bills on timeThis helps you maintain a good credit score and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. You can also set up automatic payment or payment reminders to help you pay your bill before due date. You should also opt for paying your dues in full and not just the minimum amount due in order to avoid interest charges.Use your Credit Card points and offersUsing available offers and rewards is an excellent way to maximise the benefits of your Credit Card and save money on every purchase. What is Credit Card? A Credit Card allows you to borrow money for your purchases and is like a short-term loan from a bank. Also known as plastic money, you can use this card to buy things and have the option to pay the borrowed money back all at once or in smaller amounts over time. However, if you don't pay the full amount right away, you are charged an extra amount on it in the form of interest. 2. What is the minimum credit score for a credit card? The credit card limit, which is set by the bank, represents the maximum amount you can spend using your credit card. It is determined by considering various factors such as income, age, credit history, credit score, liabilities, etc. It is essential to ensure that the total expenditure, including fees, stays within this predetermined limit. Initially, new credit card users might receive lower limits because the bank is not familiar with their spending and repayment habits. While the credit card limit can be increased, the decision ultimately rests with the bank." 3. There is no single fixed limit for all cards; it's a unique amount for each cardholder that can be checked by logging into the Mobile Banking App, open or internet banking and navigating to the account summary or control center. To know about the maximum limit on the credit card, read https://www.axis.bank.in/blogs/credit-card/what-is-maximum-credit-limit-on-a-credit-card 16. Will using a credit card affect my credit score? Yes, using a credit card can impact your credit score positively or negatively, depending on how you manage it. Here’s how: Positive impact:Timely payments: Paying your credit card bills on or before the due date improves your credit history and boosts your score. Low credit utilization: Keeping your spending well below your credit limit (ideally under 30%) shows responsible usage. Long-term usage: Maintaining a credit card account for a long time adds to your credit history length, which is good for your score. Negative impact: Late or missed payments: Delays in payment can significantly reduce your score and attract penalties. High credit utilization: Consistently using most of your credit limit may signal financial stress and lower your score. Multiple new cards: Applying for too many cards in a short period can lead to hard inquiries, which may temporarily reduce your score. Key Tip: Using a credit card responsibly is one of the easiest ways to build and maintain a healthy credit score. Always pay on time and keep your utilization low. 17. Is it shopping, dining, entertainment, fuel, travel or a combination of these categories? The ideal or best Credit Card for you therefore would be the one that is tailored to your requirements in terms of your spending habits, lifestyle goals and the credit limit you are seeking. The ultimate aim is to optimise available rewards and benefits while also considering applicable fees and interest rates.If you are a first time Credit Card holder, consider the following factors before choosing your Credit Card:Monthly expenses: Choose a Credit Card whose limit is close to your monthly expenses. If you have a lower credit limit, prioritise only the payments which should be made through your Credit Card.Rewards & Points: You could also select a Credit Card that offers certain additional benefits such as cashback and discounts on your purchases or complimentary access to airport lounges.Card control: Choose the card issuer based on how easy it is to manage the Credit Card especially on the mobile app or website. You should be able to manage spend limit, international usage, set the PlN, view payment history & statements, block & replace card, among other features.Card offers: Apart from offers from brands and merchants, card issuers also offer other benefits such as converting spends into EMIs, availing instant loans, upgrading card limit, getting an add-on card for your family members, and much more.Card fees and charges: Credit Cards will have slightly different interest rates depending on the issuer that offers the card. Therefore, always compare the fees and interest rates before you choose a Credit Card.Things to know before applying for a Credit CardIf you are a first time Credit Card holder or are planning to apply for one, here’s what you should know before choosing your Credit Card: Monthly spends: Select a Credit Card whose credit limit aligns closely with your monthly spending.Maximising benefits: Reap maximum benefits by choosing a Credit Card that offers certain additional benefits such as cashback and discounts on your purchases or complimentary access to airport lounges.Credit Card eligibility: If you have applied for an Axis Bank Credit Card, your eligibility will depend largely on the following factors: 1. Age 2. Income 3. Residential status (whether you are an Indian resident or NRI). You will have to show documents as proof of the above mentioned eligibility conditions. Documents required will include - Age and Residential proof (PAN card, Aadhaar card, Passport or Driver’s license), income proof (Salary slips or Income Tax Returns). Additionally, the bank may also look at your credit score and credit history to determine if you are eligible for a Credit Card.Fees and Charges: Credit Cards have certain fees that vary depending on the card variant you hold. Some common Credit Card fees include joining fees, annual fees, late payment fees, over-limit penalties, cash withdrawal fees, rent transaction fees, foreign currency transaction fees, etc.Interest Rates: If you repay your Credit Card dues in full every month, before the due date, then you don’t have to pay an interest rate on your Credit Card outstanding amount. But if you carry forward any amount of your Credit Card due, then you do incur an interest rate on the pending amount. This interest rate on Credit Cards is typically between 3% and 4% monthly. Tips to manage your Credit Card expensesIf you are a first time Credit Card holder or are planning to apply for one, here’s what you should know before choosing your Credit Card:Keep an eye on your spending Consistently tracking your spending can help you resist the urge to overspend. Additionally, you can set transaction limits using the “manage spends” feature for specific purchases on your Credit Card, making it easier for you to adhere to your spending objectives. Don’t use your entire Credit Card limitIdeally you should aim for spending not more than 30% of your Credit Card limit. You can control your spending and avoid debt by doing so.Check Credit Card statements regularlyRegularly checking your statement helps you stay on top of your spending, ensure accurate billing, detect fraudulent activity and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. Pay your Credit Card bills on timeThis helps you maintain a good credit score and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. You can also set up automatic payment or payment reminders to help you pay your bill before due date. You should also opt for paying your dues in full and not just the minimum amount due in order to avoid interest charges.Use your Credit Card points and offersUsing available offers and rewards is an excellent way to maximise the benefits of your Credit Card and save money on every purchase. What is Credit Card? A Credit Card allows you to borrow money for your purchases and is like a short-term loan from a bank. Also known as plastic money, you can use this card to buy things and have the option to pay the borrowed money back all at once or in smaller amounts over time. However, if you don't pay the full amount right away, you are charged an extra amount on it in the form of interest. 2. What is the minimum credit score for a credit card? The credit card limit, which is set by the bank, represents the maximum amount you can spend using your credit card. It is determined by considering various factors such as income, age, credit history, credit score, liabilities, etc. It is essential to ensure that the total expenditure, including fees, stays within this predetermined limit. Initially, new credit card users might receive lower limits because the bank is not familiar with their spending and repayment habits. While the credit card limit can be increased, the decision ultimately rests with the bank." 3. What does 'minimum due' mean on a credit card statement? The minimum amount due on a credit card represents a mandatory partial payment of the total outstanding bill, required when the entire bill amount cannot be paid.This amount is usually fixed at 2% of the total outstanding balance, calculated based on the credit card statement issued. 5. To keep your card safe, follow the below measures:Keep Track of Mailing SchedulesIf you do not receive your Axis Bank Credit Card/ Statement on the scheduled date, call the bank immediately.Keep track of your Credit Card expiry date.Incase of non-receipt; please ensure with the Bank that the dispatch is being done to your correct mailing address.Prevent Misuse:As soon as you receive your new Credit Card, sign on the signature panel.Destroy your old Credit Card by cutting it diagonally through the chip and magnetic stripe.Report loss of your Credit Card immediately to the Axis Bank Customer Care Center.Do not handover your Credit Card to anyone other than the merchant when making a payment.Safe Storage:Keep your Credit Card in the same place in your wallet/purse, so that you notice immediately if it is missing. What is a credit card limit? The credit card limit is the maximum amount you can spend on your credit card and is set by the bank. Yes, using a credit card can impact your credit score positively or negatively, depending on how you manage it. Here’s how: Positive impact:Timely payments: Paying your credit card bills on or before the due date improves your credit history and boosts your score. Low credit utilization: Keeping your spending well below your credit limit (ideally under 30%) shows responsible usage. Long-term usage: Maintaining a credit card account for a long time adds to your credit history length, which is good for your score. Negative impact: Late or missed payments: Delays in payment can significantly reduce your score and attract penalties. High credit utilization: Consistently using most of your credit limit may signal financial stress and lower your score. Multiple new cards: Applying for too many cards in a short period can lead to hard inquiries, which may temporarily reduce your score. Key Tip: Using a credit card responsibly is one of the easiest ways to build and maintain a healthy credit score. Always pay on time and keep your utilization low. 17. Is it shopping, dining, entertainment, fuel, travel or a combination of these categories? The ideal or best Credit Card for you therefore would be the one that is tailored to your requirements in terms of your spending habits, lifestyle goals and the credit limit you are seeking. The ultimate aim is to optimise available rewards and benefits while also considering applicable fees and interest rates.If you are a first time Credit Card holder, consider the following factors before choosing your Credit Card:Monthly expenses: Choose a Credit Card whose limit is close to your monthly expenses. You should be able to manage spend limit, international usage, set the PlN, view payment history & statements, block & replace card, among other features.Card offers: Apart from offers from brands and merchants, card issuers also offer other benefits such as converting spends into EMIs, availing instant loans, upgrading card limit, getting an add-on card for your family members, and much more.Card fees and charges: Credit Cards will have slightly different interest rates depending on the issuer that offers the card. Age 2. Income 3. Residential status (whether you are an Indian resident or NRI). You will have to show documents as proof of the above mentioned eligibility conditions. Documents required will include - Age and Residential proof (PAN card, Aadhaar card, Passport or Driver’s license), income proof (Salary slips or Income Tax Returns). Additionally, the bank may also look at your credit score and credit history to determine if you are eligible for a Credit Card.Fees and Charges: Credit Cards have certain fees that vary depending on the card variant you hold. Some common Credit Card fees include joining fees, annual fees, late payment fees, over-limit penalties, cash withdrawal fees, rent transaction fees, foreign currency transaction fees, etc.Interest Rates: If you repay your Credit Card dues in full every month, before the due date, then you don’t have to pay an interest rate on your Credit Card outstanding amount. But if you carry forward any amount of your Credit Card due, then you do incur an interest rate on the pending amount. This interest rate on Credit Cards is typically between 3% and 4% monthly. Tips to manage your Credit Card expensesIf you are a first time Credit Card holder or are planning to apply for one, here’s what you should know before choosing your Credit Card:Keep an eye on your spending Consistently tracking your spending can help you resist the urge to overspend. Don’t use your entire Credit Card limitIdeally you should aim for spending not more than 30% of your Credit Card limit. Pay your Credit Card bills on timeThis helps you maintain a good credit score and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. What is Credit Card? A Credit Card allows you to borrow money for your purchases and is like a short-term loan from a bank. Also known as plastic money, you can use this card to buy things and have the option to pay the borrowed money back all at once or in smaller amounts over time. However, if you don't pay the full amount right away, you are charged an extra amount on it in the form of interest. 2. What is the minimum credit score for a credit card? The credit card limit, which is set by the bank, represents the maximum amount you can spend using your credit card. It is determined by considering various factors such as income, age, credit history, credit score, liabilities, etc. It is essential to ensure that the total expenditure, including fees, stays within this predetermined limit. Initially, new credit card users might receive lower limits because the bank is not familiar with their spending and repayment habits. While the credit card limit can be increased, the decision ultimately rests with the bank." 3. What does 'minimum due' mean on a credit card statement? The minimum amount due on a credit card represents a mandatory partial payment of the total outstanding bill, required when the entire bill amount cannot be paid.This amount is usually fixed at 2% of the total outstanding balance, calculated based on the credit card statement issued. 5. Yes, using a credit card can impact your credit score positively or negatively, depending on how you manage it. Here’s how: Positive impact:Timely payments: Paying your credit card bills on or before the due date improves your credit history and boosts your score. Low credit utilization: Keeping your spending well below your credit limit (ideally under 30%) shows responsible usage. Long-term usage: Maintaining a credit card account for a long time adds to your credit history length, which is good for your score. Negative impact: Late or missed payments: Delays in payment can significantly reduce your score and attract penalties. High credit utilization: Consistently using most of your credit limit may signal financial stress and lower your score. Multiple new cards: Applying for too many cards in a short period can lead to hard inquiries, which may temporarily reduce your score. Key Tip: Using a credit card responsibly is one of the easiest ways to build and maintain a healthy credit score. Always pay on time and keep your utilization low. 17. What is Credit Card? A Credit Card allows you to borrow money for your purchases and is like a short-term loan from a bank. Also known as plastic money, you can use this card to buy things and have the option to pay the borrowed money back all at once or in smaller amounts over time. However, if you don't pay the full amount right away, you are charged an extra amount on it in the form of interest. 2. What is the minimum credit score for a credit card? The credit card limit, which is set by the bank, represents the maximum amount you can spend using your credit card. It is determined by considering various factors such as income, age, credit history, credit score, liabilities, etc. It is essential to ensure that the total expenditure, including fees, stays within this predetermined limit. Initially, new credit card users might receive lower limits because the bank is not familiar with their spending and repayment habits. While the credit card limit can be increased, the decision ultimately rests with the bank." 3. To read more click on https://www.axis.bank.in/blogs/credit-card/what-is-credit-card-limit-and-how-to-increase-your-credit-limit 15. Is there a fixed limit for all cards? There is no single fixed limit for all cards; it's a unique amount for each cardholder that can be checked by logging into the Mobile Banking App, open or internet banking and navigating to the account summary or control center. To know about the maximum limit on the credit card, read https://www.axis.bank.in/blogs/credit-card/what-is-maximum-credit-limit-on-a-credit-card 16. Will using a credit card affect my credit score? Yes, using a credit card can impact your credit score positively or negatively, depending on how you manage it. Here’s how: Positive impact:Timely payments: Paying your credit card bills on or before the due date improves your credit history and boosts your score. Low credit utilization: Keeping your spending well below your credit limit (ideally under 30%) shows responsible usage. Long-term usage: Maintaining a credit card account for a long time adds to your credit history length, which is good for your score. Negative impact: Late or missed payments: Delays in payment can significantly reduce your score and attract penalties. High credit utilization: Consistently using most of your credit limit may signal financial stress and lower your score. Multiple new cards: Applying for too many cards in a short period can lead to hard inquiries, which may temporarily reduce your score. Key Tip: Using a credit card responsibly is one of the easiest ways to build and maintain a healthy credit score. Always pay on time and keep your utilization low. 17. Mobile Banking App, open: Step 1: Login to the Mobile Banking App, open and go to the ‘Credit Card’ option. Step 2: Choose your credit card and click on the ‘Total Control’ option. Step 3: Tap on the ‘Manage Usage’ option. Step 4: Finally, choose the ‘International’ option and turn on the ‘International Usage’ option. Your credit card is now ready to be used internationally. Net banking: Step 1: Login and click on Services > Credit Card Services. Step 2: Post this, select your credit card and click on ‘Manage Usage’ option. Then you can enable international transactions for your credit card here. 7. How to prepare for international use? Enable international transactions: For new cards, you must enable online, contactless, and international transaction functionalities through the Mobile Banking App, open, internet banking, or by contacting customer support before your travel. Check for fees:Understand the foreign transaction fees and Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) fees on your specific card. For example, some cards have a DCC markup fee of 1% plus taxes on transactions in INR at international locations. Avoid restricted transactions: You cannot use the card for payments to overseas Forex trading platforms, as this is prohibited by regulations. Note on Nepal and Bhutan: Your credit card is not valid for making foreign currency transactions in Nepal and Bhutan. 8. What to expect when using your card abroad? Foreign transaction fee: A fee is often charged by the credit card network for currency conversion. Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) fee: If the merchant offers to charge you in your home currency (INR), you may be subject to a DCC fee, which is often higher than using the foreign currency directly. It is generally better to be charged in the local currency and let your bank handle the conversion. Cash advances: Taking cash from overseas ATMs can incur extra charges and higher interest rates. Taxes: Be aware that taxes may apply to international fees like DCC markup fees. 9. What are the credit card international transaction fees? To understand about the fee and breakdown, read https://www.axis.bank.in/blogs/credit-card/foreign-transaction-fee-on-credit-cards 10. What are the charges for a foreign transaction? The amount of the foreign transaction fee on credit card varies depending on the credit card issuer. Typically, this fee ranges from 1% to 3% of the transaction amount. To know more, visit: https://www.axis.bank.in/blogs/credit-card/foreign-transaction-fee-on-credit-cards Load More 1. What are the possible billing cycle dates for my credit card? The possible billing cycle dates for a credit card statement are as follows: Miles & More Cards – 25th of each month Vistara Cards – 22nd of each month Signature Card – 18th of each month Ace Credit Card – 15th of each month Axis Bank Freecharge Plus Credit Card – 12th of each month Other Cards - 1st,12th,13th,15th,20th,22nd and 25th of every month Miles & More Cards, Flipkart Axis Bank Credit Cards, Ace Credit Card, Axis Bank Freecharge Plus Credit Card & Signature Cards have a fixed billing cycle, other card customers can call us on Phone Numbers 1860-419-5555 (Charges Applicable)/ 1860-500-5555 (Charges Applicable) / 1800-103-5577 (Toll Free Number) or write to us to request for a change in the billing cycle considering the available options. 2. Credit Card billing cycle - What is it and how does it work? To know more about credit card billing cycle, visit https://www.axis.bank.in/blogs/credit-card/credit-card-billing-cycle 3. How do you check your specific billing date? To check your billing cycle date, you can go for one of the following:Axis Bank Mobile App, open or Internet Banking: Log in to Axis Bank Mobile App, open and view your account details and billing cycle information.Customer Care: Call or write to customer support to get information about your specific billing date. Statement: Your statement will show your billing cycle and due date. Load More 1. How to report a lost card? You can report a lost Axis Bank card by calling the 24-hour helpline at +91-22-67987700, using the Axis Mobile App, open or Internet Banking, or by sending an SMS to 5676782 or +919717000002 from a registered number with the message "BLOCKXXXX" (where XXXX are last 4 digits of the card number). By phone: Emergency Helpline: Call +91-22-67987700 from any phone to report the loss. Customer Service (For Forex Card): Call 1800-108-5577 (toll-free) or +91 040 67174100. By mobile or internet banking: Axis Mobile App, open: Log in to the Axis Mobile App, open and go to the credit cards section using ‘quick links’, use the "Block and replace Card" option. Internet Banking: Log in to your Internet Banking account and go to the "Credit Cards" section to block the card. By SMS: SMS format: Send "BLOCKCARD" to 5676782 or +919717000002. Important: Ensure you are using a mobile number that is registered with your Axis Bank account. 2. How do I block my card? If your credit card is lost or stolen, you can block your credit card and order for a replacement by simply entering your registered mobile number. Go to https://application.axis.bank.in/WebForms/axis-support/Block-cccard.aspx and fill in the details. If your debit card is lost or stolen, you can block your debit card and order for a replacement by simply entering your registered mobile number. Go to https://application.axis.bank.in/webforms/axis-support/block-dccard.aspx and fill in the details. 3. What should I do when my credit card is lost? In the event of losing your credit card, promptly notify Axis Bank by contacting customer care. The card will be instantly blocked, and during the same call, you can request a replacement. Additionally, report the lost card to the police station in the area where you suspect it was misplaced or lost. 4. How to block a card if it is lost/stolen? You can block a lost or stolen Axis Bank card by calling the 24/7 customer care number, sending an SMS from your registered mobile number, logging in to Mobile Banking App, open or using net banking. For debit cards, you can SMS "BLOCKCARD" to 5676782 or +919717000002. For credit cards, SMS "BLOCKXXXX" (where XXXX are the last four digits) to 5676782. By phone: Call the customer service helpline: For a debit card, call +91-22-67987700. For a Forex card, call +91 04067174100. Inform the executive: State that you want to block your card and provide the necessary details for verification. By SMS: For debit cards: Type BLOCK CARD and send it to 5676782 or +919717000002 from your registered mobile number. For credit cards: Type BLOCK XXXX (where XXXX is the last four digits of your card) and send it to 5676782 from your registered mobile number. Online: Mobile Banking App, open: Log in to the app to find the option to block your card. Net Banking: Access your account through Axis Bank's website and use the card blocking feature under the card services section. 5. What to do after blocking my card? Once the card is blocked, you can apply for a replacement card through your bank branch, as blocking the card doesn't automatically order a new one. Is it shopping, dining, entertainment, fuel, travel or a combination of these categories? The ideal or best Credit Card for you therefore would be the one that is tailored to your requirements in terms of your spending habits, lifestyle goals and the credit limit you are seeking. The ultimate aim is to optimise available rewards and benefits while also considering applicable fees and interest rates.If you are a first time Credit Card holder, consider the following factors before choosing your Credit Card:Monthly expenses: Choose a Credit Card whose limit is close to your monthly expenses. If you have a lower credit limit, prioritise only the payments which should be made through your Credit Card.Rewards & Points: You could also select a Credit Card that offers certain additional benefits such as cashback and discounts on your purchases or complimentary access to airport lounges.Card control: Choose the card issuer based on how easy it is to manage the Credit Card especially on the mobile app or website. You should be able to manage spend limit, international usage, set the PlN, view payment history & statements, block & replace card, among other features.Card offers: Apart from offers from brands and merchants, card issuers also offer other benefits such as converting spends into EMIs, availing instant loans, upgrading card limit, getting an add-on card for your family members, and much more.Card fees and charges: Credit Cards will have slightly different interest rates depending on the issuer that offers the card. Therefore, always compare the fees and interest rates before you choose a Credit Card.Things to know before applying for a Credit CardIf you are a first time Credit Card holder or are planning to apply for one, here’s what you should know before choosing your Credit Card: Monthly spends: Select a Credit Card whose credit limit aligns closely with your monthly spending.Maximising benefits: Reap maximum benefits by choosing a Credit Card that offers certain additional benefits such as cashback and discounts on your purchases or complimentary access to airport lounges.Credit Card eligibility: If you have applied for an Axis Bank Credit Card, your eligibility will depend largely on the following factors: 1. Age 2. Income 3. Residential status (whether you are an Indian resident or NRI). You will have to show documents as proof of the above mentioned eligibility conditions. Documents required will include - Age and Residential proof (PAN card, Aadhaar card, Passport or Driver’s license), income proof (Salary slips or Income Tax Returns). Additionally, the bank may also look at your credit score and credit history to determine if you are eligible for a Credit Card.Fees and Charges: Credit Cards have certain fees that vary depending on the card variant you hold. Some common Credit Card fees include joining fees, annual fees, late payment fees, over-limit penalties, cash withdrawal fees, rent transaction fees, foreign currency transaction fees, etc.Interest Rates: If you repay your Credit Card dues in full every month, before the due date, then you don’t have to pay an interest rate on your Credit Card outstanding amount. But if you carry forward any amount of your Credit Card due, then you do incur an interest rate on the pending amount. This interest rate on Credit Cards is typically between 3% and 4% monthly. Tips to manage your Credit Card expensesIf you are a first time Credit Card holder or are planning to apply for one, here’s what you should know before choosing your Credit Card:Keep an eye on your spending Consistently tracking your spending can help you resist the urge to overspend. Additionally, you can set transaction limits using the “manage spends” feature for specific purchases on your Credit Card, making it easier for you to adhere to your spending objectives. Don’t use your entire Credit Card limitIdeally you should aim for spending not more than 30% of your Credit Card limit. You can control your spending and avoid debt by doing so.Check Credit Card statements regularlyRegularly checking your statement helps you stay on top of your spending, ensure accurate billing, detect fraudulent activity and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. Pay your Credit Card bills on timeThis helps you maintain a good credit score and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. You can also set up automatic payment or payment reminders to help you pay your bill before due date. You should also opt for paying your dues in full and not just the minimum amount due in order to avoid interest charges.Use your Credit Card points and offersUsing available offers and rewards is an excellent way to maximise the benefits of your Credit Card and save money on every purchase. What is Credit Card? A Credit Card allows you to borrow money for your purchases and is like a short-term loan from a bank. Also known as plastic money, you can use this card to buy things and have the option to pay the borrowed money back all at once or in smaller amounts over time. Yes, using a credit card can impact your credit score positively or negatively, depending on how you manage it. Here’s how: Positive impact:Timely payments: Paying your credit card bills on or before the due date improves your credit history and boosts your score. Low credit utilization: Keeping your spending well below your credit limit (ideally under 30%) shows responsible usage. Long-term usage: Maintaining a credit card account for a long time adds to your credit history length, which is good for your score. Negative impact: Late or missed payments: Delays in payment can significantly reduce your score and attract penalties. High credit utilization: Consistently using most of your credit limit may signal financial stress and lower your score. Multiple new cards: Applying for too many cards in a short period can lead to hard inquiries, which may temporarily reduce your score. Key Tip: Using a credit card responsibly is one of the easiest ways to build and maintain a healthy credit score. Always pay on time and keep your utilization low. 17. Don’t use your entire Credit Card limitIdeally you should aim for spending not more than 30% of your Credit Card limit. You can control your spending and avoid debt by doing so.Check Credit Card statements regularlyRegularly checking your statement helps you stay on top of your spending, ensure accurate billing, detect fraudulent activity and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. Pay your Credit Card bills on timeThis helps you maintain a good credit score and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. You can also set up automatic payment or payment reminders to help you pay your bill before due date. You should also opt for paying your dues in full and not just the minimum amount due in order to avoid interest charges.Use your Credit Card points and offersUsing available offers and rewards is an excellent way to maximise the benefits of your Credit Card and save money on every purchase. What is Credit Card? A Credit Card allows you to borrow money for your purchases and is like a short-term loan from a bank. Also known as plastic money, you can use this card to buy things and have the option to pay the borrowed money back all at once or in smaller amounts over time. However, if you don't pay the full amount right away, you are charged an extra amount on it in the form of interest. 2. What is the minimum credit score for a credit card? The credit card limit, which is set by the bank, represents the maximum amount you can spend using your credit card. It is determined by considering various factors such as income, age, credit history, credit score, liabilities, etc. It is essential to ensure that the total expenditure, including fees, stays within this predetermined limit. Initially, new credit card users might receive lower limits because the bank is not familiar with their spending and repayment habits. To know about the maximum limit on the credit card, read https://www.axis.bank.in/blogs/credit-card/what-is-maximum-credit-limit-on-a-credit-card 16. Will using a credit card affect my credit score? Yes, using a credit card can impact your credit score positively or negatively, depending on how you manage it. Here’s how: Positive impact:Timely payments: Paying your credit card bills on or before the due date improves your credit history and boosts your score. Low credit utilization: Keeping your spending well below your credit limit (ideally under 30%) shows responsible usage. Long-term usage: Maintaining a credit card account for a long time adds to your credit history length, which is good for your score. Negative impact: Late or missed payments: Delays in payment can significantly reduce your score and attract penalties. High credit utilization: Consistently using most of your credit limit may signal financial stress and lower your score. Multiple new cards: Applying for too many cards in a short period can lead to hard inquiries, which may temporarily reduce your score. Key Tip: Using a credit card responsibly is one of the easiest ways to build and maintain a healthy credit score. Always pay on time and keep your utilization low. 17. If you have a lower credit limit, prioritise only the payments which should be made through your Credit Card.Rewards & Points: You could also select a Credit Card that offers certain additional benefits such as cashback and discounts on your purchases or complimentary access to airport lounges.Card control: Choose the card issuer based on how easy it is to manage the Credit Card especially on the mobile app or website. You should be able to manage spend limit, international usage, set the PlN, view payment history & statements, block & replace card, among other features.Card offers: Apart from offers from brands and merchants, card issuers also offer other benefits such as converting spends into EMIs, availing instant loans, upgrading card limit, getting an add-on card for your family members, and much more.Card fees and charges: Credit Cards will have slightly different interest rates depending on the issuer that offers the card. Therefore, always compare the fees and interest rates before you choose a Credit Card.Things to know before applying for a Credit CardIf you are a first time Credit Card holder or are planning to apply for one, here’s what you should know before choosing your Credit Card: Monthly spends: Select a Credit Card whose credit limit aligns closely with your monthly spending.Maximising benefits: Reap maximum benefits by choosing a Credit Card that offers certain additional benefits such as cashback and discounts on your purchases or complimentary access to airport lounges.Credit Card eligibility: If you have applied for an Axis Bank Credit Card, your eligibility will depend largely on the following factors: 1. Age 2. Income 3. Residential status (whether you are an Indian resident or NRI). You will have to show documents as proof of the above mentioned eligibility conditions. Documents required will include - Age and Residential proof (PAN card, Aadhaar card, Passport or Driver’s license), income proof (Salary slips or Income Tax Returns). Additionally, the bank may also look at your credit score and credit history to determine if you are eligible for a Credit Card.Fees and Charges: Credit Cards have certain fees that vary depending on the card variant you hold. Some common Credit Card fees include joining fees, annual fees, late payment fees, over-limit penalties, cash withdrawal fees, rent transaction fees, foreign currency transaction fees, etc.Interest Rates: If you repay your Credit Card dues in full every month, before the due date, then you don’t have to pay an interest rate on your Credit Card outstanding amount. But if you carry forward any amount of your Credit Card due, then you do incur an interest rate on the pending amount. This interest rate on Credit Cards is typically between 3% and 4% monthly. Tips to manage your Credit Card expensesIf you are a first time Credit Card holder or are planning to apply for one, here’s what you should know before choosing your Credit Card:Keep an eye on your spending Consistently tracking your spending can help you resist the urge to overspend. Additionally, you can set transaction limits using the “manage spends” feature for specific purchases on your Credit Card, making it easier for you to adhere to your spending objectives. Don’t use your entire Credit Card limitIdeally you should aim for spending not more than 30% of your Credit Card limit. You can control your spending and avoid debt by doing so.Check Credit Card statements regularlyRegularly checking your statement helps you stay on top of your spending, ensure accurate billing, detect fraudulent activity and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. Pay your Credit Card bills on timeThis helps you maintain a good credit score and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. You can also set up automatic payment or payment reminders to help you pay your bill before due date. You should also opt for paying your dues in full and not just the minimum amount due in order to avoid interest charges.Use your Credit Card points and offersUsing available offers and rewards is an excellent way to maximise the benefits of your Credit Card and save money on every purchase. What is Credit Card? A Credit Card allows you to borrow money for your purchases and is like a short-term loan from a bank. Also known as plastic money, you can use this card to buy things and have the option to pay the borrowed money back all at once or in smaller amounts over time. However, if you don't pay the full amount right away, you are charged an extra amount on it in the form of interest. 2. What is the minimum credit score for a credit card? The credit card limit, which is set by the bank, represents the maximum amount you can spend using your credit card. It is determined by considering various factors such as income, age, credit history, credit score, liabilities, etc. It is essential to ensure that the total expenditure, including fees, stays within this predetermined limit. Initially, new credit card users might receive lower limits because the bank is not familiar with their spending and repayment habits. While the credit card limit can be increased, the decision ultimately rests with the bank." 3. What does 'minimum due' mean on a credit card statement? The minimum amount due on a credit card represents a mandatory partial payment of the total outstanding bill, required when the entire bill amount cannot be paid.This amount is usually fixed at 2% of the total outstanding balance, calculated based on the credit card statement issued. 5. Yes, using a credit card can impact your credit score positively or negatively, depending on how you manage it. Here’s how: Positive impact:Timely payments: Paying your credit card bills on or before the due date improves your credit history and boosts your score. Low credit utilization: Keeping your spending well below your credit limit (ideally under 30%) shows responsible usage. Long-term usage: Maintaining a credit card account for a long time adds to your credit history length, which is good for your score. Negative impact: Late or missed payments: Delays in payment can significantly reduce your score and attract penalties. High credit utilization: Consistently using most of your credit limit may signal financial stress and lower your score. Multiple new cards: Applying for too many cards in a short period can lead to hard inquiries, which may temporarily reduce your score. Key Tip: Using a credit card responsibly is one of the easiest ways to build and maintain a healthy credit score. Always pay on time and keep your utilization low. 17. To know about the maximum limit on the credit card, read https://www.axis.bank.in/blogs/credit-card/what-is-maximum-credit-limit-on-a-credit-card 16. Will using a credit card affect my credit score? Yes, using a credit card can impact your credit score positively or negatively, depending on how you manage it. Here’s how: Positive impact:Timely payments: Paying your credit card bills on or before the due date improves your credit history and boosts your score. Low credit utilization: Keeping your spending well below your credit limit (ideally under 30%) shows responsible usage. Long-term usage: Maintaining a credit card account for a long time adds to your credit history length, which is good for your score. Negative impact: Late or missed payments: Delays in payment can significantly reduce your score and attract penalties. High credit utilization: Consistently using most of your credit limit may signal financial stress and lower your score. Multiple new cards: Applying for too many cards in a short period can lead to hard inquiries, which may temporarily reduce your score. Key Tip: Using a credit card responsibly is one of the easiest ways to build and maintain a healthy credit score. Always pay on time and keep your utilization low. 17. Additionally, report the lost card to the police station in the area where you suspect it was misplaced or lost. 4. How to block a card if it is lost/stolen? You can block a lost or stolen Axis Bank card by calling the 24/7 customer care number, sending an SMS from your registered mobile number, logging in to Mobile Banking App, open or using net banking. For debit cards, you can SMS "BLOCKCARD" to 5676782 or +919717000002. For credit cards, SMS "BLOCKXXXX" (where XXXX are the last four digits) to 5676782. By phone: Call the customer service helpline: For a debit card, call +91-22-67987700. For a Forex card, call +91 04067174100. Inform the executive: State that you want to block your card and provide the necessary details for verification. By SMS: For debit cards: Type BLOCK CARD and send it to 5676782 or +919717000002 from your registered mobile number. For credit cards: Type BLOCK XXXX (where XXXX is the last four digits of your card) and send it to 5676782 from your registered mobile number. Online: Mobile Banking App, open: Log in to the app to find the option to block your card. Net Banking: Access your account through Axis Bank's website and use the card blocking feature under the card services section. 5. What to do after blocking my card? Once the card is blocked, you can apply for a replacement card through your bank branch, as blocking the card doesn't automatically order a new one. Is it shopping, dining, entertainment, fuel, travel or a combination of these categories? The ideal or best Credit Card for you therefore would be the one that is tailored to your requirements in terms of your spending habits, lifestyle goals and the credit limit you are seeking. The ultimate aim is to optimise available rewards and benefits while also considering applicable fees and interest rates.If you are a first time Credit Card holder, consider the following factors before choosing your Credit Card:Monthly expenses: Choose a Credit Card whose limit is close to your monthly expenses. If you have a lower credit limit, prioritise only the payments which should be made through your Credit Card.Rewards & Points: You could also select a Credit Card that offers certain additional benefits such as cashback and discounts on your purchases or complimentary access to airport lounges.Card control: Choose the card issuer based on how easy it is to manage the Credit Card especially on the mobile app or website. You should be able to manage spend limit, international usage, set the PlN, view payment history & statements, block & replace card, among other features.Card offers: Apart from offers from brands and merchants, card issuers also offer other benefits such as converting spends into EMIs, availing instant loans, upgrading card limit, getting an add-on card for your family members, and much more.Card fees and charges: Credit Cards will have slightly different interest rates depending on the issuer that offers the card. Therefore, always compare the fees and interest rates before you choose a Credit Card.Things to know before applying for a Credit CardIf you are a first time Credit Card holder or are planning to apply for one, here’s what you should know before choosing your Credit Card: Monthly spends: Select a Credit Card whose credit limit aligns closely with your monthly spending.Maximising benefits: Reap maximum benefits by choosing a Credit Card that offers certain additional benefits such as cashback and discounts on your purchases or complimentary access to airport lounges.Credit Card eligibility: If you have applied for an Axis Bank Credit Card, your eligibility will depend largely on the following factors: 1. Age 2. Income 3. Residential status (whether you are an Indian resident or NRI). You will have to show documents as proof of the above mentioned eligibility conditions. Documents required will include - Age and Residential proof (PAN card, Aadhaar card, Passport or Driver’s license), income proof (Salary slips or Income Tax Returns). Additionally, the bank may also look at your credit score and credit history to determine if you are eligible for a Credit Card.Fees and Charges: Credit Cards have certain fees that vary depending on the card variant you hold. Some common Credit Card fees include joining fees, annual fees, late payment fees, over-limit penalties, cash withdrawal fees, rent transaction fees, foreign currency transaction fees, etc.Interest Rates: If you repay your Credit Card dues in full every month, before the due date, then you don’t have to pay an interest rate on your Credit Card outstanding amount. But if you carry forward any amount of your Credit Card due, then you do incur an interest rate on the pending amount. This interest rate on Credit Cards is typically between 3% and 4% monthly. Tips to manage your Credit Card expensesIf you are a first time Credit Card holder or are planning to apply for one, here’s what you should know before choosing your Credit Card:Keep an eye on your spending Consistently tracking your spending can help you resist the urge to overspend. Additionally, you can set transaction limits using the “manage spends” feature for specific purchases on your Credit Card, making it easier for you to adhere to your spending objectives. Don’t use your entire Credit Card limitIdeally you should aim for spending not more than 30% of your Credit Card limit. You can control your spending and avoid debt by doing so.Check Credit Card statements regularlyRegularly checking your statement helps you stay on top of your spending, ensure accurate billing, detect fraudulent activity and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. Pay your Credit Card bills on timeThis helps you maintain a good credit score and avoid late payment fees and interest charges. You can also set up automatic payment or payment reminders to help you pay your bill before due date. You should also opt for paying your dues in full and not just the minimum amount due in order to avoid interest charges.Use your Credit Card points and offersUsing available offers and rewards is an excellent way to maximise the benefits of your Credit Card and save money on every purchase. Refer Now Already a registered user? | Login to the dashboard How the Refer for Rewards program Works Earn Gift Vouchers in 3 easy steps Fill in your details and generate your Referral Link Share the Referral Link with your Friends and Family Your Friend/Family will apply on the referral link Earn Rewards on every successful Credit Card issuance Frequently Asked Questions 1. What is the Axis Bank Refer for Rewards Program? Axis Bank introduces an online Credit Card Referral Program. You can refer your friends and family to apply for a new Axis Bank Credit Card through this program. If Axis Bank issues a credit card to the referred person, you will receive reward points from ₹500 - ₹1,000 which can be used to redeem gift vouchers on every referral you make through your referral link only. A person who is referring his/her friends will now is termed as “Referrer” and the person getting referred for Axis Bank Credit Card is termed as “Referee”. 2. Who is eligible under the Axis Bank Credit Card Referral Program? Anyone, whether they are an existing customer of Axis bank or not, is eligible to refer their friends and family. The Axis group (Axis Bank and its subsidiaries) employees can refer their friends and family, but they won’t be eligible to earn referral reward vouchers. To know more about the program, please refer to the terms and conditions. 3. What is the Referral Reward? On every successful credit card referral (A ‘successful credit card referral’ means that the referred person has applied according to the terms of the campaign and has been issued a credit card by Axis Bank) through this referral program, the referrer will receive Gift Vouchers. The Gift vouchers will depend upon the Card Type issued to the referee as listed in the below table: Credit Card Variant Gift Vouchers in ₹ Rewards 500 My Zone 500 Indian Oil 500 Flipkart 500 Samsung Signature 500 Neo 500 Shoppers Stop 500 Cashback 500 Ace 500 Indigo 500 Credit Card Variant Gift Vouchers in ₹ Privilege 750 Rewards 750 SpiceJet Voyage Black 750 Magnus 1000 Select 1000 Horizon 1000 Samsung Infinite 1000 Indigo Premium 1000 A referral is considered successful only if the referred person applies using your unique referral link and is issued a credit card by Axis Bank in accordance with the campaign terms. 4. How to refer under the Axis Bank Referral Program? The referral program is completely digital. Referrer can register to the Referral portal via Axis Bank Website or the referral link: https://refer.axis.bank.in/retail/cards/credit-card/refer-and-earn/index.htm. Already registered user can also login through the Dashboard link: https://refer.axis.bank.in/retail/cards/credit-card/refer-and-earn/dashboard/Login.aspx Steps to Refer: - 1) Referrer to register on referral link https://refer.axis.bank.in/retail/cards/credit-card/refer-and-earn/index.htm by entering their full name, email ID and Mobile number. If already registered, then can login with their user id and password. 2) Upon Login, referrer will be able to view their unique referral code/link and they can choose to share with their friends and family via various social media channels - WhatsApp, LinkedIn, Twitter, Email or by copying the referral link. 3) The Referee upon receiving the invitation from the referrer will click on the invitation link and fill in the required details to apply for Axis Bank Credit Card. Referrer can earn Gift Vouchers up to ₹10,000 in a calendar year and the reward will only be given in case the credit card gets issued to the referee. 5. How to avail the Reward/Vouchers? The reward value will be reflecting on the referrer’s account within 60 working days after the referee’s credit card is issued. The referral reward will have to be claimed by the referrer by logging into the Referral Portal Dashboard: https://refer.axis.bank.in/retail/cards/credit-card/refer-and-earn/dashboard/Login.aspx 1) Post Login on the dashboard, referrer to click on the ‘Redeem’ button. 2) Here, the Referrer will be able to view Vouchers of different brands – BookMyShow, Flipkart, Myntra, Swiggy, Domino’s Pizza. 3) Referrer will then select the required voucher basis the Reward value/points. 4) Once the referrer confirms on the order the voucher code will be shared via SMS/Email communication. 6. What do the statuses in the referral dashboard indicate? There are 4 statuses in the referral dashboard: A) Not Applied Yet: The referee has not applied through your referral link yet. This means that if the referees have applied from some other link/source and not through your own referral link, the status would still be shown as 'Not Applied Yet’. B) Applied/ Under Process: This status is updated once a week. C) Approved: This status is updated once a week and the referees who have been successfully approved will have their statuses reflected in the dashboard only in the forthcoming week. D) Not Approved: This status is updated weekly once and the referees whose application has not been approved will have their statuses reflected in the dashboard only in the forthcoming week. The reason for the same will be sent via email to the referee’s registered email-id. This communication will not be sent to the referrer. 7.
